text: Which country currently holds the largest stock of US Treasury securities outside the United States itself?
explanation: Japan (~$1.1T) overtook China around 2022. China has been reducing its holdings.

text: The Thucydides Trap — the theory that a rising power and an established power are likely to go to war — was coined by which scholar?
explanation: Graham Allison at Harvard coined the term and examined 16 historical cases in 'Destined for War' (2017).

text: Under UNCLOS, the Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled in 2016 that China's claims in the South China Sea were invalid. What was China's response?

options.A: It accepted the ruling and withdrew claims
options.B: It ignored and rejected the ruling as illegitimate
options.C: It appealed to the UN Security Council
options.D: It filed a counter-claim at the ICJ

explanation: China declared the ruling 'null and void' and has continued its activities in the region.

text: NATO's Article 5 collective defence clause has been formally invoked exactly once. When?

options.D: It has never been formally invoked

explanation: Article 5 was invoked on 12 September 2001, the day after the 9/11 attacks.

text: China's Belt and Road Initiative originally had a different name. What was it?
explanation: It was launched as 'One Belt One Road' (OBOR) in 2013 before being rebranded BRI.

text: Which five countries hold permanent veto power on the UN Security Council?
explanation: The P5 are the US, UK, France, Russia (USSR seat), and China (PRC took ROC seat in 1971).

text: The 1916 Sykes-Picot Agreement secretly divided which region between British and French spheres of influence?
explanation: Britain and France carved up the Ottoman Middle East, drawing borders that still define the region today.

text: Which sovereign wealth fund is the world's largest by assets under management?
explanation: Norway's GPFG (~$1.6T) is the world's largest SWF, owning roughly 1.5% of all global equities.

text: Which central bank was the first to implement a sustained negative interest rate policy?
explanation: The Riksbank cut its repo rate to -0.25% in February 2015 and sustained it; the ECB followed months later.

text: The 2008 financial crisis spread globally primarily because banks held what instruments rated AAA that were backed by subprime mortgages?
explanation: CDO tranching gave AAA ratings to subprime-backed securities; banks worldwide held them, spreading the contagion.

text: The Bretton Woods system collapsed in 1971. What specific action by Nixon caused the immediate break?
explanation: Nixon's 'gold window' closure — ending dollar-gold convertibility at $35/oz — ended the fixed exchange rate system.

text: What does an inverted yield curve (short rates above long rates) historically signal?
explanation: An inverted yield curve has preceded every US recession since 1955, typically by 12–18 months.

text: In a currency carry trade, an investor profits by doing what?

options.A: Buying a currency before central bank intervention
options.B: Borrowing in a low-interest currency and investing in a high-interest currency
options.C: Shorting a currency during a current account deficit

explanation: The carry trade exploits interest rate differentials; it unwinds violently when risk sentiment turns.

text: George Akerlof's 'The Market for Lemons' (1970), which won a Nobel Prize, introduced which concept?
explanation: Akerlof showed that information asymmetry causes adverse selection — good cars exit the market, only lemons remain.

text: Quantitative easing (QE) primarily affects the economy through which mechanism?

options.C: Central bank asset purchases that lower long-term yields and push investors into risk assets

explanation: QE compresses long yields by buying bonds, pushing investors toward equities and credit, and signalling low rates ahead.

text: The Black-Scholes options pricing model assumes which of the following?

options.C: Asset prices follow geometric Brownian motion with constant volatility

explanation: Black-Scholes assumes log-normal prices, constant volatility, and continuous trading — all simplifications reality violates.

text: Rust guarantees memory safety without a garbage collector through which compile-time system?
explanation: Rust's ownership rules and borrow checker enforce that each value has one owner; borrows are checked at compile time.

text: A Byzantine fault-tolerant system can operate correctly even if some nodes do what?

options.C: Send arbitrary or maliciously incorrect messages

explanation: Byzantine faults include arbitrary/malicious behavior, not just crashes. BFT consensus (e.g., PBFT) tolerates up to f failures in 3f+1 nodes.

text: The CAP theorem states a distributed system cannot simultaneously guarantee Consistency, Availability, and what third property?
explanation: Eric Brewer's CAP theorem: in a network partition, a system must choose between consistency and availability.

text: What is the key difference between TCP and UDP?

options.A: TCP is faster; UDP is slower
options.B: TCP guarantees ordered, reliable delivery; UDP does not
options.C: UDP is encrypted; TCP is not
options.D: TCP is for video; UDP is for text

explanation: TCP handshakes, acknowledges, and retransmits. UDP is fire-and-forget — lower latency, no delivery guarantee.

text: Public key cryptography (RSA) relies on the computational difficulty of which mathematical problem?

options.A: Solving large systems of linear equations
options.B: Computing discrete logarithms in elliptic curves
options.C: Factoring the product of two large prime numbers

explanation: RSA security depends on the fact that multiplying large primes is easy; factoring their product is computationally infeasible.

text: The 'attention mechanism' in transformer models (the basis of GPT, BERT etc.) does what?

options.A: Filters irrelevant tokens with a threshold
options.B: Computes weighted relationships between all token pairs in a sequence
options.C: Applies convolutional filters across token windows

explanation: Self-attention scores every token's relationship with every other token, enabling long-range dependencies without recurrence.

text: Which misfolded protein is central to the propagation of Parkinson's disease between neurons?
explanation: Alpha-synuclein aggregates into Lewy bodies and can spread prion-like between neurons.

text: Why does the James Webb Space Telescope primarily observe in infrared rather than visible light?

options.A: Infrared passes through Earth's atmosphere more easily
options.B: Distant objects are redshifted into infrared, and infrared penetrates dust
options.C: Visible light sensors are too expensive
options.D: Infrared has higher resolution than visible light

explanation: Cosmological redshift moves ancient starlight into infrared; infrared also pierces dust clouds that block visible light.

text: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing works by using the Cas9 protein as what?

options.A: A viral vector for gene delivery
options.C: A molecular scissor guided by RNA to cut specific DNA sequences
options.D: A repair template for homologous recombination

explanation: Guide RNA directs Cas9 to a specific DNA sequence where it makes a double-strand break, allowing edits.

text: mRNA vaccines (like Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine) work by doing what inside your cells?

options.B: Inserting viral DNA into your genome
options.C: Instructing ribosomes to produce a viral protein that triggers an immune response

explanation: mRNA is translated by ribosomes into the spike protein; the immune system learns to recognise it without any live virus.

text: Why does quantum entanglement NOT allow faster-than-light communication?

options.A: Entangled particles are always too far apart
options.B: Measuring one particle gives a random result — you cannot control what it shows
options.D: Only photons can be entangled, and photons travel at light speed

explanation: Measurement outcomes are random. You can't encode information in a random result, so no signal is transmitted.

text: Dark matter has not been directly detected despite strong indirect evidence. Which of the following is NOT a proposed detection method?

options.A: Looking for recoil of atomic nuclei in underground detectors
options.D: Detecting dark matter radio emissions with standard antennas

explanation: Direct detection (nuclear recoil), indirect detection (annihilation products), and gravitational methods are all serious approaches. Radio emission is not a standard proposed method.

text: The 1973 Arab oil embargo was triggered by US support for which country in which conflict?

options.A: Israel in the Yom Kippur War

explanation: OAPEC imposed the embargo after the US resupplied Israel during the October 1973 Yom Kippur (Ramadan) War.

text: Which article of the Treaty of Versailles assigned sole war guilt to Germany, enabling massive reparations?
explanation: Article 231 — the 'war guilt clause' — was the legal basis for ~132 billion gold marks in reparations.

text: The Cuban Missile Crisis (1962) ended when the Soviets agreed to remove missiles from Cuba in exchange for what?

options.A: The US paying reparations to Cuba
options.B: The US publicly pledging not to invade Cuba and secretly removing Jupiter missiles from Turkey
options.C: Cuba joining the Warsaw Pact formally
options.D: The US lifting its trade embargo on Cuba

explanation: The public deal was a US non-invasion pledge; the secret concession was removing US Jupiter missiles from Turkey.

text: The Marshall Plan (1948) had a primary strategic goal beyond economic recovery. What was it?

options.B: Preventing the spread of communism by stabilising Western European democracies
options.D: Establishing US military bases across Europe

explanation: Truman and Marshall explicitly designed the plan to counter Soviet influence by making capitalism visibly succeed in Western Europe.

text: The Nixon Shock of 1971 ended the Bretton Woods system. Which country had been putting the most pressure on US gold reserves by demanding redemption?
explanation: De Gaulle's France was famously converting dollar reserves to gold, sailing ships to collect it — accelerating the crisis.

text: The Rwandan genocide of 1994 was primarily carried out by Hutu extremists against which group?
explanation: Approximately 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu were killed in roughly 100 days in one of history's fastest genocides.

text: Socrates said 'The unexamined life is not worth living.' In what context?

options.A: In his philosophical dialogues with Plato
options.B: At his trial when offered exile instead of death

explanation: He said it at his trial in 399 BC, choosing death over abandoning philosophy — recorded in Plato's Apology.

text: John Rawls's 'veil of ignorance' thought experiment asks us to design a just society under what condition?

options.A: Knowing your own talents but not others'
options.B: Not knowing your place in society, class, or natural abilities
options.C: Assuming everyone is equal in ability
options.D: Designing for the worst-off member only

explanation: The veil of ignorance strips away knowledge of your own position, forcing principles you'd accept from any position.

text: Marshall McLuhan's phrase 'the medium is the message' means what?

options.A: The content of media determines its cultural impact
options.B: The form/channel of communication shapes society more than its content
options.C: Television is more powerful than radio
options.D: Messages are always distorted in transmission

explanation: McLuhan argued that electric light — contentless — transforms society more profoundly than anything transmitted through it.

text: The Dunning-Kruger effect describes the tendency of people with limited knowledge to do what?
explanation: Kruger and Dunning (1999) showed that incompetent people lack the metacognitive ability to recognise their own incompetence.

text: The Overton window describes what in political theory?

options.A: The gap between public opinion and policy outcomes
options.B: The range of policies currently acceptable to the mainstream public
options.C: The time lag between elections and policy change

explanation: Joseph Overton's concept: only policies inside this window are politically viable; activists shift the window to make new ideas acceptable.

text: Which philosopher argued that we cannot step into the same river twice — meaning reality is constant flux?
explanation: Heraclitus (~500 BC): 'You cannot step into the same river twice, for new waters are always flowing.' Being is becoming.
